claims.claim: Vancouver's four-day advance voting total was a preliminary 103,810.
claims.episode_span: preliminary figures put advance turnout at 103,810 across four days
claims.source_title: Vancouver advance voting period ends with nearly 104,000 voters after four record-breaking days
claims.supporting_quote: The preliminary counts of the four advance voting days add up to 103,810 voters.

claims.claim: 29,096 people voted in Vancouver on October 13, 2026, a single-day advance record, after 21,824 on October 3, 25,142 on October 7 and 27,748 on October 10.
claims.episode_span: Tuesday, October 13, drew 29,096 voters, a new single-day early-voting record
claims.source_title: Vancouver advance voting period ends with nearly 104,000 voters after four record-breaking days
claims.supporting_quote: Participation climbed steadily throughout the advance voting period, from 21,824 on Oct. 3 to 25,142 on Oct. 7 and 27,748 on Oct. 10, before reaching Oct. 13’s new high.

claims.claim: Advance turnout was about 60 per cent higher than roughly 65,000 advance voters in 2022, and about 61 per cent of 171,494 ballots cast in the entire 2022 civic election.
claims.episode_span: about 60 per cent above roughly 65,000 advance voters in the 2022 civic election
claims.source_title: Vancouver advance voting period ends with nearly 104,000 voters after four record-breaking days
claims.supporting_quote: According to the City, overall advance voting participation increased by approximately 60 per cent compared with roughly 65,000 voters in the 2022 civic election’s advance voting period.

claims.claim: Vancouver's main civic voting day is Saturday, October 17, with 85 locations open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
claims.episode_span: Main voting day is Saturday, October 17, with 85 locations open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
claims.source_title: Vancouver advance voting period ends with nearly 104,000 voters after four record-breaking days
claims.supporting_quote: The civic election’s main voting day is Saturday, Oct. 17, when 85 voting locations will be open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

claims.claim: Justice Dickson granted an interim injunction pausing Vancouver Aquatic Centre demolition until November 3, 2026, the day after the park board's November 2 inaugural meeting.
claims.episode_span: Justice Dickson has granted an interim injunction halting further demolition
claims.source_title: Appeal court pauses Vancouver Aquatic Centre demolition until early November
claims.supporting_quote: However, the injunction is highly temporary — running until Nov. 3, 2026, just one day after the newly elected Vancouver Park Board’s inaugural meeting, scheduled for Nov. 2.

claims.claim: A September Supreme Court ruling allowed the City to use $103 million in 2022 borrowing for a 25-metre pool concept, and the approved design is a $175-million complex.
claims.episode_span: use $103 million in 2022 voter-approved borrowing for a 25-metre concept
claims.source_title: Appeal court pauses Vancouver Aquatic Centre demolition until early November
claims.supporting_quote: That separate case centred on whether the municipal government could use $103 million in borrowing approved by voters — in the capital plan plebiscite question held during the 2022 civic election — to replace the aquatic centre with a facility containing a 25-metre lap pool.

claims.claim: Heatherbrae Builders received a $3.5-million demolition contract in July 2026; the centre opened in 1974, closed June 28, 2026, and demolition had been scheduled for October 1.
claims.episode_span: A $3.5-million demolition contract went to Heatherbrae Builders in July
claims.source_title: Appeal court pauses Vancouver Aquatic Centre demolition until early November
claims.supporting_quote: While a $3.5-million contract was awarded to Heatherbrae Builders in July 2026 to carry out the demolition work, the municipal government has yet to award the substantial contract to build the brand-new complex.

claims.claim: The only scheduled B.C. leaders' debate before the October 24 election is tonight from 6:15 p.m. to 8 p.m., moderated by Shachi Kurl.
claims.source_title: Watch the B.C. election provincial leaders’ debate live
claims.supporting_quote: It is the only scheduled leaders’ debate leading up to the B.C. election on Oct. 24 and it takes place tonight starting at 6:15 p.m.

claims.claim: Mike Starchuk said Rob Stutt chaired the May 29 meeting that moved to terminate Norm Lipinski and should say whether he told Brenda Locke the purpose beforehand.
claims.episode_span: Starchuk said councillor Rob Stutt, of Locke's Surrey Connect party, chaired that meeting
claims.source_title: Incumbent mayor Brenda Locke under renewed scrutiny over termination of Surrey police chief
claims.supporting_quote: Surrey mayoral candidate Mike Starchuk noted Tuesday that councillor Rob Stutt, a member of Locke’s Surrey Connect party, was chair of the May 29 meeting and needs to address whether he ever spoke to Locke about the purpose of the meeting ahead of time.

claims.claim: Surrey Connect said Mayor Locke has no involvement in HR matters and that SPS staff decisions are made by the police board.
claims.episode_span: Surrey Connect said Locke has no involvement in human-resources matters
claims.source_title: Incumbent mayor Brenda Locke under renewed scrutiny over termination of Surrey police chief
claims.supporting_quote: “Mayor Locke has no involvement in HR matters. All staff decisions at the SPS are made by the Surrey police board, which is independent of the city and the mayor,” the party stated.

claims.claim: A judge on Tuesday dismissed a B.C. NDP petition questioning at least one Vancouver-Yaletown candidate over nomination forms alleged to contain questionable names and signatures.
claims.episode_span: dismissed a B.C. NDP petition that questioned the legitimacy of at least one candidate in Vancouver-Yaletown
claims.source_title: Judge dismisses B.C. NDP's challenge of Green party candidate in Yaletown riding
claims.supporting_quote: A petition filed in B.C. Supreme Court by the B.C. NDP questioning the legitimacy of at least one candidate in Vancouver-Yaletown for the provincial election was dismissed by a judge on Tuesday.

claims.claim: Sixty Surrey firefighters raised $25,000 for Muscular Dystrophy Canada this year, bringing Local 1271's lifetime contribution to $266,000, and won the 2026 Dr. David Green Award, to be presented in Ottawa in November.
claims.episode_span: Sixty Surrey firefighters raised $25,000 for Muscular Dystrophy Canada this year
claims.source_title: Surrey Firefighters win MDC's Fire Department of the Year
claims.supporting_quote: Sixty firefighters raised $25,000 for MDC this year, taking Surrey Local 1271’s lifetime contribution to the charity to $266,000.

claims.claim: No weather watches or warnings are in effect; current conditions are light rain and 11.1 degrees, with Wednesday rain ending near noon and a high of 15.
claims.episode_span: No weather watches or warnings are in effect. It is light rain and 11.1 degrees now
claims.supporting_quote: No watches or warnings in effect.

claims.claim: Highway 99 paving in Vancouver runs overnight Wednesday and Thursday from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., with northbound single-lane alternating traffic and southbound open to buses and emergency vehicles only.
claims.episode_span: On Highway 99 in Vancouver, paving runs tonight and Thursday from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m.
claims.source_title: DriveBC: 8 major road events in Metro Vancouver
claims.supporting_quote: From 11:00 PM to 5:00 AM PDT the next day, Wednesday and Thursday. Single lane alternating traffic.

claims.claim: The Islanders beat the Canucks 3-2, and Kyle Palmieri scored his first two goals of the season.
claims.episode_span: The New York Islanders beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2 on Tuesday
claims.source_title: Palmieri scores first two goals of season, Islanders edge Canucks
claims.supporting_quote: Palmieri scores first two goals of season, Islanders edge Canucks

claims.claim: Leevi Meriläinen made 18 saves in the third period, and Brock Boeser said he kept the Canucks in the game.
claims.episode_span: Leevi Meriläinen made 18 saves in the third period alone.
claims.source_title: I Watched This Game: Meriläinen stands on head as Canucks extend losing streak
claims.supporting_quote: The 24-year-old goaltender made 18 saves in the third period alone to give his teammates a chance to push the game to overtime, even if they couldn’t quite get it there.
